sentences.text:
Before discussing the grounds on which a review is sought for, it would be necessary to have the brief resume of facts which had led to the filing of the writ petition, and the same is as under :
a) The above writ petition has been filed by the petitioner herein seeking a mandamus to respondents 1 to 5 to take action to cancel the documents viz., (i) the Power of Attorney Deed dated 02.08.1991, registered as Doc.No.1239/Book 4/1991,
on the file of the SRO, Anna Nagar; (ii) the sale deed dated 21.01.1993 registered as C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141509610/
2 Doc.No.262/1993 on the file of SRO, Anna Nagar; (iii) sale deed dated 30.10.2009,
registered as Doc.No.3321 of 2009 on the file of SRO, Villivakkam, as fraudulent documents and therefore to direct the fifth respondent to execute the sale deed in respect of the subject property in favour of the petitioners and to direct the sixth respondent to permit the petitioner to withdraw the compensation of Rs 26,55,199/-
deposited towards acquisition of a portion of the property.
b) It is their case that one Chandrasekaran, husband of the first petitioner and father of the second petitioner, had been allotted the subject property by the Tamil Nadu Housing Board on 20.02.1987.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025

sentences.text: The said Chandrasekaran was not keeping good health and ultimately, he died on 24.08.2010.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: During his lifetime, he was informed by the Housing Board about the plot allotted to him and since he was not keeping good health, he was not able to execute the sale deed in his name.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Taking advantage of his illness, a local politician had hatched a plan to grab the property and in furtherance of this, a Power of Attorney dated 02.08.1991 was created as if the said Chandrasekaran had given power to the seventh respondent herein, to act on his behalf.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: On 21.01.1993, the Tamil Nadu Housing Board executed a sale deed in favour of Chandrasekaran with regard to the subject property.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: c) Thereafter, the seventh respondent claiming to be the Power Agent of Chandrasekaran, had executed a sale deed dated 30.10.2009, in favour of his wife, the eighth respondent herein.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: d) Thereafter, the Highways Department had acquired 28 sq.mtr., in Plot No.1294 (originally measuring 956 sq.ft.).
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The 8th respondent filed a claim petition to receive the compensation amount, to which an objection was raised.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: It was also brought to the notice of the Highways Department that there were some impersonation in the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 Power of Attorney and about the subsequent sale deeds and hence, the compensation amount of Rs.16,61,219/- was directed to be deposited in Court.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The original compensation amount has been further enhanced to a sum of Rs.26,55,199/- and the difference amount was also deposited in Court.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: e) The petitioners had learnt that the respondents 7 and 8 are taking steps to withdraw the said compensation and hence, they made a complaint to the District Registrar Administration, the third respondent herein, for enquiring into the documents.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Ultimately, the third respondent had sent the Power of Attorney document for the opinion of hand-writing expert, who on perusal, had opined that the signature was not of Chandrasekaran.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
f) The petitioner would contend that the respondents 7 and 8 had played fraud to grab the property,
by colluding with the officials of the Housing Board, the fifth respondent herein, and when this impersonation was brought to the notice of the respondents 1 to 4, no action was taken by them to date.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Therefore, the petitioner left with no other alternative, has approached this Court in W.P.No.36434 of 2014 seeking a mandamus viz., (i) to cancel the https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis (
Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 Power of Attorney Deed dated 02.08.1991 and also to cancel the subsequent sale that had taken place between the 7th C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141509610/
3 and 8th respondent; (ii) to direct the fifth respondent to execute a sale deed in their favour with respect to the subject property at Plot No.1294, 72nd Street, Korattur, Chennai; and (iii) to direct the 6th respondent to permit them to withdraw the compensation amount lying in court deposit.
g) This Court by an order dated 22.01.2025, had dismissed the said writ petition.
Hence, the petitioner are now before this Court to review the said order.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners has drawn reference to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Asset Reconstruction Company (India) Limited Vs. S.P.Velayutham and Others reported in (2022) 8 SCC 210.
4.

sentences.text: When the writ petition came up for hearing on 22.01.2025, this Court had taken note of the fact that the relief sought by the writ petitioners was to cancel the alleged documents, and this Court, in the light of the judgment https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 reported in M.Kathhirvel Vs. Inspector of General of Registration, Department of Registration and Others reported in 2024 (4) CTC 769, held that the said relief could not be granted, as the Sub Registrar's right of cancellation of document, has been held unconstitutional, and dismissed the writ petition, however, this Court granted liberty to the petitioners to exhaust their other legal remedies available to them.

entities.text: M.Kathhirvel Vs. Inspector of General of Registration, Department of Registration and Others reported in 2024 (4) CTC 769
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 5. The petitioners without proceeding to have their title declared with respect to the subject property, have filed this review petition, on the ground that the facts of the present case was covered by the judgment in Asset Reconstruction Company (India) Limited Vs. S.P.Velayutham and Others.

entities.text: Asset Reconstruction Company (India) Limited Vs. S.P.Velayutham and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
That however was a case where title suits were already pending between the parties, despite which,
the writ jurisdiction was sought to be invoked on the ground that the original Power of Attorney, on the strength of which, the sale that had taken place, did not confer a power of sale on the the power agent.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The Hon'ble Supreme Court held that the Sub Registrar was bound to verify the documents presented by any person mentioned under Section 32 of the Registration Act.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Since the document in question in Asset Reconstruction Company case cited supra, was presented by Power of Attorney,
the Hon'ble https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 Supreme Court has held that the registering authority is bound to verify as to whether the agent had the right to execute the document.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
The Hon'ble Supreme Court has observed as follows in the said judgment :
"49
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: . ..... ...... ...... We are concerned in this case with the most fundamental question whether the registering authority could have turned a blind eye to the fact that the deed of PoA on the basis of which the sale deed was executed as well as presented for registration by S.P.Velayutham contained an express prohibition for the power agent to create an encumbrance on the property, especially in the light of the Rules framed under Section 69 of the Act."
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: 6. However, in the case on hand, the review petitioners seek to set aside the Power of Attorney dated 02.08.1991 and the two sale deeds dated 21.01.1993 and 30.10.2009.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text:
Of these two sale deeds, the C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141509610/
4 sale deed dated 21.01.1993 was executed in favour of Chandrasekaran by the Tamil Nadu Housing Board, under whom the petitioners claim a right.

entities.text: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: If the sale deed in favour of Chandrasekaran is sought to be assailed, then the petitioners who are claiming title under Chandrasekaran, on the basis of an allotment letter issued in favour of the Chandrasekaran, cannot challenge the same.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: That apart, they would have no locus standi to question the documents.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Further, Chandrasekaran, in whose favour the allotment had been made in the year https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 1987, had died only in the year 2010, and the Power of Attorney Deed, which sought to be cancelled, is executed in the year 1991.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: There is no explanation as to why Chandrasekaran himself has not sought to have his allotment converted into a sale deed, after all these years till his death i.e., from 1987 to 2010, whereas even during his lifetime, the sale deed has been executed in his favour.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The right of the Sub Registrar to cancel the deeds have been held unconstitutional in the M.Kathhirvel case.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: Therefore, the relief claimed could not be granted.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: While dismissing the writ petition, this Court had directed the petitioner to avail the other legal remedies available to them.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: However, the petitioner without taking steps to avail the remedies available to them, have chosen to file the present review petition.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: The petitioners have not made out any case that there is error apparent on the face of the records of this Court in W.P.No.36434 of 2024 or that they have come into knowledge of a position of law or documents thereafter.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

sentences.text: In the guise of this review petition, the petitioners are only seeking to re-argue the case and establish title without approaching the civil Court especially when third party rights have set in as early as in the year 1991.
sentences._hearing_file: C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025.json

opennyai_summary.facts:
The said Chandrasekaran was not keeping good health and ultimately, he died on 24.08.2010.
During his lifetime, he was informed by the Housing Board about the plot allotted to him and since he was not keeping good health, he was not able to execute the sale deed in his name.
On 21.01.1993, the Tamil Nadu Housing Board executed a sale deed in favour of Chandrasekaran with regard to the subject property.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
3. The learned counsel appearing for the petitioners has drawn reference to the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Asset Reconstruction Company (India) Limited Vs. S.P.Velayutham and Others reported in (2022) 8 SCC 210.
4.
opennyai_summary.issue: . ..... ...... ...... We are concerned in this case with the most fundamental question whether the registering authority could have turned a blind eye to the fact that the deed of PoA on the basis of which the sale deed was executed as well as presented for registration by S.P.Velayutham contained an express prohibition for the power agent to create an encumbrance on the property, especially in the light of the Rules framed under Section 69 of the Act."
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Of these two sale deeds, the C.Vasanthakumari vs The Inspector General Of Registration on 10 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141509610/
4 sale deed dated 21.01.1993 was executed in favour of Chandrasekaran by the Tamil Nadu Housing Board, under whom the petitioners claim a right.
If the sale deed in favour of Chandrasekaran is sought to be assailed, then the petitioners who are claiming title under Chandrasekaran, on the basis of an allotment letter issued in favour of the Chandrasekaran, cannot challenge the same.
That apart, they would have no locus standi to question the documents.
Further, Chandrasekaran, in whose favour the allotment had been made in the year https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 29/08/2025 08:54:56 pm ) Review Application No.162 of 2025 1987, had died only in the year 2010, and the Power of Attorney Deed, which sought to be cancelled, is executed in the year 1991.
The right of the Sub Registrar to cancel the deeds have been held unconstitutional in the M.Kathhirvel case.
Therefore, the relief claimed could not be granted.
While dismissing the writ petition, this Court had directed the petitioner to avail the other legal remedies available to them.
The petitioners have not made out any case that there is error apparent on the face of the records of this Court in W.P.No.36434 of 2024 or that they have come into knowledge of a position of law or documents thereafter.
opennyai_summary.10_July_2025__decision:
However, the petitioner without taking steps to avail the remedies available to them, have chosen to file the present review petition.
In the guise of this review petition, the petitioners are only seeking to re-argue the case and establish title without approaching the civil Court especially when third party rights have set in as early as in the year 1991.
The review application is accordingly dismissed.
